title: Land secured for South Auckland hospital
summary: Land has been secured for a future hospital facility on Karaka Road in Drury, marking a significant investment in the long-term healthcare needs of South Auckland's growing population.

title: Pharmacies to provide more funded medicines
summary: Pharmac and Health New Zealand are increasing the number of funded medicines community pharmacies can provide from today, Associate Health Minister David Seymour and Health Minister Simeon Brown say.

title: Government progresses plan changes to enable growth for New Plymouth
summary: Targeted changes to New Plymouth’s District Plan will make it easier for homeowners and developers to build, alter homes, and make better use of land, while removing unnecessary consenting requirements and other planning barriers to growth.

title: Next steps for Nelson Tasman weather radar
summary: Nelson Tasman communities are one step closer to more timely and accurate weather information, with a site selected for the region’s new weather radar.

title: Beekeepers get more certainty on American foulbrood management
summary: The Government is progressing long-signalled updates to the National American Foulbrood Pest Management Plan, based on proposals developed and consulted on by the beekeeping industry.

title: Working capital grants for regional airlines
summary: The Regional Infrastructure Fund will provide funding to help regional airlines manage the operating pressures facing the sector.

title: Dry dock project moves to expert consideration
summary: The Northland Shipyard and Dry Dock project has had its Fastrack application accepted as complete by the Environmental Protection Authority.

title: New appointment to Māori language Commission
summary: Dr Julian Wilcox has been appointed Chair of the Māori Language Commission for a three-year term, effective 5 October 2026. He brings extensive expertise in te reo Māori, governance, broadcasting and public-sector leadership. Acting Māori Development Minister Shane Jones also thanked outgoing Chair

title: Taking $14.6 million off criminals to protect New Zealanders
summary: Money seized from criminals will fund nine initiatives to reduce violence, prevent reoffending, and disrupt the drug trade, says Associate Justice Minister Nicole McKee.

title: Regulation Ministry sets sites on building sector
summary: Regulation Minister David Seymour and Building and Construction Minister Simon Watts have today announced the Ministry for Regulation’s next Regulatory Review will be into the building and construction sector.

title: Resilience investment in key Waikato freight link
summary: A major Waikato transport route will receive government funding for the replacement of a nearly century-old bridge.

title: Queenstown cable car gets lift through AIP visa
summary: The Queenstown Cable Car project led by Southern Infrastructure Limited (SIL) has attracted $265 million in private lending through the Government’s Active Investor Plus (AIP) visa, Infrastructure Minister Chris Bishop and Immigration Minister Erica Stanford say.

title: Govt funds new classrooms at Wakatipu High School
summary: The Government is investing in new classrooms at Wakatipu High School to address the rapidly growing demand in Queenstown for secondary education, Education Minister Erica Stanford and Infrastructure Minister Chris Bishop say.

title: Otago Central Lakes Deal signed to back growth
summary: The Government has signed a City and Regional Deal with Otago Central Lakes councils, establishing a 10-year partnership to support housing, infrastructure and economic growth in one of New Zealand’s fastest-growing regions, Infrastructure Minister Chris Bishop and Local Government Minister Simon Wa

title: Strategic plan sets direction for Queenstown transport
summary: A 30-year strategic plan released today by the NZ Transport Agency (NZTA) will help focus ongoing investment in Queenstown’s transport infrastructure into the right areas, at the right time and help keep people moving, Transport Minister Chris Bishop says.
